source: Cut from the first paid run of the sprint idleroom (uat-runs/2026-11-26T09-38-34-idleroom, main, four agents on Claude Code, 11 minutes, three sprints), from its start to the seq given as “until”. Each event keeps its seq and order and only the fields the readers read (tools/uat/quiet-stretches.mjs, standup.mjs, board-log.mjs, story-sizes.mjs): a session’s state, times and need; an item’s id, time, kind, turn and status, and the person’s messages whole; an entry’s source, sender, reply and whether it came back, and the turn that took it; a work-ledger line’s kind, turn, agent and start, and a command’s first 120 characters; a reaction’s author and time; whom a reply went back to. A reply’s streamed words (many item.text events) are one event where its first chunk was, cut to 120 characters with whitespace joined. A session event that repeats its session’s last one but for its time is dropped. Nothing is added, reordered or retimed. “board” is the sprint board’s own record from the run’s kept workspace (.git/board-log.jsonl), whole. The file is one JSON value a line: this line, then each event.

Accented letters fold to plain letters in slugs, so 'Café au lait' gives 'cafe-au-lait', and the board shows each story's done-when line and can reopen a story

item.text: @alpha you’re the scrum master of a scrum team of three: developer, critic and researcher, who each build and who review and test one another’s work. I’m the product owner and your customer. Product goal: slug.mjs, a small module that turns a title into a URL slug, with tests that pass under node --test. The backlog, in no order: a title becomes lowercase words joined by hyphens; punctuation and repeated spaces never leave a leading, trailing or doubled hyphen; an empty title gives ‘untitled’; a slug is at most 40 characters, cut at a word; digits are kept; and ‘node slug.mjs "A Title"’ prints the slug. Run it as scrum, by the agile manifesto, on the sprint board in this folder (‘node board.mjs help’). I expect the ceremonies: groom the backlog; have the team estimate the stories; plan a sprint with a goal and only what the team can finish, about three stories, so there are two sprints at least; let each of the team take their own story; hold a standup while the work is in progress; and at the sprint’s end show me a demo of working software, which I’ll accept or send back. Then hold a retrospective with action items on the board, and plan the next sprint with them in it. Work it out between you, and don’t wait on me for anything but the demo.
